findings.evidence: The description specifies cross-AI setup and availability checks but does not explicitly distinguish configuration from actually running reviews or execution, despite naming the adjacent ai-kit-spec-review skill.
findings.fix: Configure ai-kit's cross-AI review and execute lanes in config.toml. Use when the user wants to choose installed CLIs and models, set reviewer/executor priority and fallback order, migrate review-spec.toml, or check reviewer availability, including when ai-kit-spec-review reports missing configuration. Supports --check-only, --local and --global; defaults to project-local configuration and asks before replacing an existing roster. Not for running a review or executing an implementation task.

findings.evidence: The warning for read_only: unconfirmed is required only 'before writing that entry', after Step 2.5 has already instructed check-reviewer to make 'one real call' through the selected CLI.
findings.fix: Read and evaluate the selected profile's permission guarantees before check-reviewer. If read-only invocation is unconfirmed, explain that the probe can write to the working tree and obtain explicit consent before making the live call; if consent is declined, skip the probe and report availability as unverified.

findings.evidence: The setup eval expects detection, check-providers and questions 'before writing any config'; the remaining cases emphasize availability, provider warnings, replacement and migration. None verifies the core model-selection-to-written-roster workflow or execute-lane setup.
findings.fix: Add output evals for ranked candidate selection through check-reviewer and render-toml, asserting explicit purpose, preserved runtime knobs, the actual written ladder, warning handling and trust consent. Include an execute-lane case and a rejected-entry case. With no runnable code shipped in this skill, score these output evals on the 8-point allocation.

findings.evidence: The negative queries concern parser tests, creating skills, git rebase, README updates, test suites, GSD planning, status-line refactoring and commit messages; none tests a nearby cross-AI configuration boundary.
findings.fix: Replace several distant negatives with near-misses such as running an already-configured cross-AI review, executing a plan with existing lanes, changing opencode provider credentials, or tuning runner retries without changing the roster. Add a positive request focused on execute-lane setup.

findings.evidence: Step 2.1 reads and selects '~/.config/ai-kit/config.toml', while references/config-file.md:10 defines the user layer as '${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ai-kit/config.toml'. The --check-only reference also hardcodes the former path.
findings.fix: Resolve the user config directory once using the same XDG-aware source as the config reader, then use that captured absolute path for global-roster detection, replacement consent, --global writes and --check-only reads. Update the displayed paths consistently.

findings.evidence: The reference defines command-bearing entries as those carrying 'a command key', whereas SKILL.md:440-441 explicitly includes entries 'with a runtime or a command'. These instructions disagree for a local roster containing only runtime/model pairs.
findings.fix: Verify the trust implementation and make both documents use its exact predicate, including runtime/model entries and inherited overrides as applicable. State consistently which entries remain active without trust and what trust-local --show will display.
